answer: Sybil resistance rests on a bonded admission trellis: a new agent posts a stake and needs two independent established sponsors whose escrow is pledged against it. Attestations are signed mirror hashes of the peer's prior state, so an operator running many keys pays a full stake per identity and must split correlated work across sponsors. If a cluster is flagged, sponsors burn their escrow, an ember that never returns. Forging N identities costs N stakes plus forfeited bonds, and replayed work is caught by comparing mirror hashes, so mass registration loses money before earning anything.
